Subject: Next steps — long-history eval kit, benchmarks & truncation risks

Thanks again for the demo time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (1-line): WellPath is looking to auto-summarize multi-year patient visit histories (visit notes + meds + labs) into structured care summaries for care management and HCC coding support. The primary concerns you raised were truncation of long histories, summarization fidelity for edge cases (complex comorbid patients), and latency constraints for near-real-time workflows.

What we recommend for an initial evaluation (what we'll deliver):
- Eval kit: prompt-suite-v1.jsonl (30 canonical prompts + 200 example records), evaluation harness, and benchmark CSV with baseline metrics (attached).
- Models to test: Redwood-recommended long-window variants: Llama3-70B-XL 64k quantized (for fidelity), Mistral-Instruct-30B 32k, and Llama2-13B-chat-extended (lower-cost baseline). We'll surface quantization tradeoffs in the report.
- Metrics: ROUGE-L, BERTScore, and a small human-rating rubric (faithfulness, hallucination, truncation-impact).

Immediate asks from WellPath to run the kit: 
1) Small sample export: 200 de-identified patient histories (realistic distribution across chronic/acute profiles).
2) Confirm preferred secure upload method (SFTP or secure Drive).
3) Any disallowed PHI fields so we can sanitize accordingly.

Known risks / caveats: 
- Long-window models mitigate token truncation but are still sensitive to KV cache eviction patterns for extremely long sequences — we expect occasional context drop in >50k token inputs without hierarchical pre-summarization.
- Summarization fidelity degrades on nested temporal reasoning unless prompts include explicit timeline anchors (we've included examples in the prompt set).

Proposed timeline:
- Within 48h: We send the full eval kit (prompts + harness + baseline benchmarks).
- Week 1: WellPath provides sample export and we run initial pass.
- Week 2: Joint review + 30-min technical deep dive to discuss results and model tradeoffs.

Attached: long-history-benchmarks.csv, prompt-suite-v1.jsonl, mutual-action-plan-WELL-4821.docx

Appreciate a quick confirmation on the upload method and whether the 200-record sample is feasible this week.

Cheers,

Liam / team — quick answers and technical notes from the SE side: 

1) Benchmark CSV example: each row = test_id, input_length_tokens, model, config, rouge_l, bertscore, human_faithfulness(1-5), truncation_flag (true/false), notes. We'll attach a sample row in drive. Fields are intentionally minimal so you can map them into your analytics.

2) PHI handling: Redwood supports no-persistence runs (ephemeral runtime) for hosted trials and customer-managed KMS for Private deployments. We can also sign an SOP addendum. We'll note this in the MAP.

3) Latency guidance: in Redwood Dedicated with optimized kernels and batching tuned for streaming, we typically see 95th percentile per-token latencies of ~0.6–0.9ms on A100x GPU instances for the quantized Llama3-70B-64k path (this translates to ~1.5s for generating ~1k tokens, but real-world varies with batching and prefix lengths). For clients with strict <1s SLOs, we recommend either a smaller model or a hybrid path (short-path LLM + async deep-summarize).

Notes on truncation and mitigation strategies: 
- KV cache eviction: very long single-pass inputs can force older KV segments out. Mitigations: hierarchical chunking (summarize older segments into compact summaries before ingest), sliding-window attention, or model-side prefix caching. Our eval harness includes a hierarchical-summarizer baseline you can toggle.
- Prompting: timeline anchors and explicit "most recent first" ordering reduce hallucination; see prompt-suite examples 12–18.
- Quality metrics: we recommend combining automated metrics above with a 50-case human spot-check focusing on medication lists and temporal order.

Links: sample benchmark row + example eval run are here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-longhistory-benchmarks and s3://redwood-evals/wellpath/long-history/benchmarks-v1.csv

If you want, we can run a short smoke test on a synthetic subset you provide before you upload any de-identified PHI.

—Ben
